correctness.rationale: The binary proof was checked lemma by lemma. In the local bubble lemma, the two binary boundary symbols need only be unequal to the edited symbol, so arbitrary q-ary run boundaries work. The remaining alphabet-dependent counts replace 2^d by q^d and one recorded bit by one recorded q-ary symbol; for fixed q these change only constants. The witness, hashing, support-component and bipartition arguments are alphabet-independent, yielding redundancy (2t-1) log_q n + O_{q,t}(log log n).

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. En Gad's 16 September 2026 preprint proves the coefficient 2t-1 for binary codes and explicitly asks whether it holds for fixed larger alphabets. Exact and synonymous searches found no prior fixed-q theorem with this coefficient. Earlier q-ary two-deletion constructions found in the search have larger leading redundancy. The recency of the motivating preprint leaves a substantial simultaneous-work risk.

value.rationale: The result closes an explicit open extension question and shows that the new one-power-of-n gain is not binary-specific. For t=2 it gives fixed-q existential codes with leading redundancy 3 log_q n instead of the classical greedy coefficient 4.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
